sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports the ramp and wave functions
sections.what: Imports the ramp function, the window length constant, the wave functions and the wave length constant.
sections.why: The docstring says these two stages decide how much benefit lands, and the tests use the real functions.
sections.watch_out: Renaming any of these functions breaks every test in this file.

sections.name: TestTheRampIsNotAStepChange
sections.title: Checks the adoption ramp with known values
sections.what: Checks that an instant start realises the whole window, a ramp equal to the window realises half, a longer ramp realises less, a start after the window realises nothing, later starts and longer ramps never realise more, and a negative ramp is refused.
sections.why: The docstring says the mutation this guards is replacing the curve with full benefit everywhere, which would make a six-month ramp realise a full year.
sections.watch_out: The expected values depend on the window length, so changing it changes several figures at once.

sections.name: TestWavesComeFromTheGraph
sections.title: Checks waves come from the dependency graph
sections.what: Checks that processes with no dependencies are wave one, chains add waves, the longest path sets a process's wave, an outside prerequisite pushes its successor back, edges to processes outside the portfolio are ignored, cycles are refused, starts are spaced by the wave length, and groups are ordered.
sections.why: The docstring says taking the first edge would start a process before its second prerequisite lands, and an early version ignored outside prerequisites and produced one flat wave.
sections.watch_out: The rule that an outside prerequisite counts as a real step means any missing platform changes the wave plan, so removing that rule would change results broadly.

summary: Checks the adoption ramp, which sets how fast a benefit reaches full effect, and the wave plan, which groups processes into start waves based on their dependencies.
purpose: Makes sure the ramp and the wave grouping give the expected figures, because together they decide how much of a benefit lands within the analysis window.
why: The docstring says both are pure functions of named constants, so they can be checked exactly rather than approximately.
how: 1) Checks the ramp against known values: an instant start realises the whole window, a ramp equal to the window realises half, longer ramps realise less, late starts realise less, and a negative ramp is refused. 2) Checks wave numbers from a dependency graph: independent processes are wave one, chains add waves, the longest path decides, an outside prerequisite pushes its successor, and a cycle is refused. 3) Checks wave start months are spaced by the wave length and that grouping is ordered.
inputs: Hand-written process ids, dependency pairs, and start and ramp durations.
outputs: Pass or fail for each check.
risks: Expected figures depend on the window length and wave length constants, so changing either changes several expected results at once. A deliberate change to the curve shape also requires updating the expected numbers.
debug: If a ramp check fails, compare the realised fraction with the expected figure and check the window length constant. If a wave check fails, look at how the wave function handles cycles and outside prerequisites. The check named for a step change describes a mutation test.
